title: Package registry: installedAt and updatedAt read as the boot time after every restart — the stored install time is not served
body:
qa#3 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibzj9DrVWXkq7joYHGB

Found by a qa#3 routine round (owed:weekly) at objectstack main 0c2aeb96, beside the clauses of `api-backend.package-rest-lifecycle` (off-clause probe, RUNNER rule 8). Severity: low. No open issue matches (searched open issues for installedAt).

## Reproduction (stock showcase, file DB, admin session)

1. `POST /api/v1/packages` with body `{"manifest":{"id":"com.example.qa-pkg-lifecycle-probe","name":"QA Probe","version":"1.0.0","scope":"project","type":"app"}}` → 201; note `installedAt` = T0.
2. Stop the server and boot it again on the same file DB.
3. `GET /api/v1/packages/com.example.qa-pkg-lifecycle-probe` → `installedAt` and `updatedAt` both equal the restart time T1, not T0. A second restart gives T2. Reproduced on two restarts.

Expected: `installedAt` (and `updatedAt` unless the package changed) are served as stored — the PATCH contract already preserves `installedAt`, so a restart re-stamping it contradicts the same door.

## Mechanism (not proven)

The boot hydration appears to re-install each `sys_packages` row through `registry.installPackage` (`packages/services/service-package/src/index.ts`), which stamps fresh lifecycle times instead of carrying the stored ones.
